simple: Above every character's head, Roblox can show a name and a health bar. This page shows how to control them with `Humanoid` properties: how far away they can be seen, when the health bar appears, whether walls hide them, and what name shows. This is handy for hiding enemy names in a stealth game, giving guards a generic name, or letting players pick a roleplay name.
analogy: It is like name tags at a big event. You can decide how close someone has to be to read your tag, whether your tag shows how tired you are, and whether people behind a wall can still see it.
keyPoints: The name and health bar only show if the `Humanoid` is inside a `Model` that also has a part named `Head`, both at the same level.
`DisplayDistanceType` decides whose distance counts: `Viewer` (the person looking), `Subject` (the character being looked at), or `None` (never show).
`NameDisplayDistance` and `HealthDisplayDistance` set how many studs away the name and health bar can be seen, such as 20 and 15.
`HealthDisplayType` can be `AlwaysOn`, `DisplayWhenDamaged`, or `AlwaysOff`. The bar goes from green to yellow to red as health drops.
`NameOcclusion` decides if walls hide the name: `NoOcclusion`, `OccludeAll`, or `EnemyOcclusion` (hidden only from players on other teams).
Walls with `Transparency` above 0.99, and other characters, do not hide names.
Change players' displays in a server Script using `PlayerAdded` and `CharacterAdded`. For NPCs, just edit the Humanoid in the Properties window.
You can set `Humanoid.DisplayName` to any name. If players type the name, send it to the server and filter it with `TextService` first.

terms.Humanoid: The object inside a character that gives it health, movement, and the name/health display.
terms.stud: Roblox's unit of distance. A default character is about 5 studs tall.
terms.Viewer: The character doing the looking. With this setting, the viewer's own distance numbers decide what they see.
terms.Subject: The character being looked at. With this setting, its own distance numbers decide who can see its name.
terms.occlusion: Being hidden because something is in the way, like a name hidden behind a stone column.
terms.line-of-sight: A straight, clear path between the camera and the character.
terms.MaxHealth: The most health a character can have, often 100. At 50 health out of 100 the bar is half full and yellow.
terms.Display Name: The friendly name on a Roblox account. It is different from the Username, which is unique and used to log in.
terms.filter: Run text through Roblox's safety check so bad words or personal info get hidden with hashtags.
terms.RemoteEvent: An object that carries a message from a player's device to the server, or back.

example.title: Show names close up and health only when hurt
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local function onCharacterAdded(character)
	local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")

	-- Each character controls who can see its own name and health
	humanoid.DisplayDistanceType = Enum.HumanoidDisplayDistanceType.Subject
	humanoid.NameDisplayDistance = 20 -- visible from 20 studs
	humanoid.HealthDisplayDistance = 15 -- health visible from 15 studs

	-- Only show the health bar when hurt
	humanoid.HealthDisplayType = Enum.HumanoidHealthDisplayType.DisplayWhenDamaged

	-- Hide names behind walls from players on other teams
	humanoid.NameOcclusion = Enum.NameOcclusion.EnemyOcclusion
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacterAdded)
end)
explain: Every time a player's character spawns, we find its `Humanoid`.
`Subject` means other players see this name only when within 20 studs of this character.
The health bar shows within 15 studs, and only when health is below max.
`EnemyOcclusion` hides the name behind walls from enemies, but teammates still see it.

watchOut: Building an NPC without a part named exactly `Head`. No name or health bar will appear.
Setting display properties only once. Characters are rebuilt when they respawn, so set them in `CharacterAdded`.
Putting a player-typed name straight onto `DisplayName`. Always filter it on the server first.
Using a see-through wall and expecting it to hide names. Walls above 0.99 transparency do not count.
